canonical.title: Containers as the containment layer for `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`

parent.title: Running Claude Code safely on a Linux workstation, and where Proxmox actually helps

siblings.title: Threat model and blast radius: what actually goes wrong running an agentic coding CLI on your workstation
siblings.summary: The realized 2026 losses come from the agent's own destructive git commands and from supply-chain malware that weaponizes an installed agent CLI — not from the exotic prompt-injection scenarios; containment must stop out-of-workspace writes, egress, and credential reads, in that order.

siblings.title: Claude Code's native guardrails in 2026: what the permission model holds, and where it stops
siblings.summary: Claude Code's permission rules are an in-process policy layer, not a security boundary; only the bubblewrap-backed Bash sandbox has OS teeth, and it covers Bash alone.

siblings.title: Linux-native sandboxing for Claude Code on the workstation itself
siblings.summary: Turn on Claude Code's built-in bubblewrap sandbox, then wrap the whole process in a 30-line bwrap script; systemd-run --user, firejail and Flatpak are the wrong tools for this job.

siblings.title: Proxmox as the isolation boundary for Claude Code: KVM VM, not LXC
siblings.summary: Use a KVM VM, never an LXC: Proxmox's own docs say containers share the host kernel and LXC upstream says privileged containers cannot be root-safe.

siblings.title: Credential isolation for an agentic coding CLI on Linux
siblings.summary: An agent that can read $HOME holds your whole identity, and on Linux the keyring does not help — so give the agent its own short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials instead.

siblings.title: Audit trail and recovery drills for an agentic coding CLI on Linux
siblings.summary: Git commits are your real undo and a PostToolUse hook is your real audit log — Claude Code's own transcripts and /rewind are convenience layers that expire, miss bash, and are writable by the agent.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Sandbox environments
sources.claim: Anthropic's own comparison of sandboxing approaches ranks VM strongest, containers medium-effort, and states --dangerously-skip-permissions should always run inside a container, VM, or sandbox runtime.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Development containers
sources.claim: The reference devcontainer is an example not a maintained image; it warns it cannot prevent exfiltration of anything in the container including ~/.claude credentials, and the CLI rejects --dangerously-skip-permissions when launched as root.

sources.title: anthropics/claude-code — .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh
sources.claim: The reference firewall script builds an ipset from GitHub's api.github.com/meta web+api+git CIDR blocks plus a handful of domains, sets INPUT/OUTPUT/FORWARD policy DROP, and allows DNS/53 and SSH/22 unconditionally.

sources.title: anthropics/claude-code issue #36907 — DNS bypass in init-firewall.sh
sources.claim: The reference firewall allows outbound UDP/53 to any resolver, so DNS tunnelling bypasses the IP allowlist entirely; the issue was closed as not planned.

sources.title: VirtusLab/sandcat
sources.claim: Sandcat wires a transparent mitmproxy via a WireGuard sidecar and shares its network namespace with the agent container, so the agent itself holds no NET_ADMIN and cannot alter the firewall; secrets are placeholder-substituted at the proxy.

sources.title: agentcage
sources.claim: agentcage runs the agent on a Podman --internal network with no gateway, plus dnsmasq and mitmproxy sidecars, and is fail-closed by default.

sources.title: Docker docs — Rootless mode
sources.claim: Rootless Docker runs daemon and containers inside a user namespace, needs 65536 subuid/subgid, does not support AppArmor, supports cgroups only on cgroup v2 + systemd, and needs CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE or a sysctl to publish ports below 1024.

sources.title: Ken Muse — Rootless Docker and its hidden security trade-offs
sources.claim: Rootless mode trades daemon-root risk for a larger unprivileged-user-namespace kernel attack surface; Qualys disclosed three bypasses of Ubuntu's unprivileged-namespace restrictions in 2025.

sources.title: arXiv 2606.08433 — comparative study of AI code sandbox engines
sources.claim: A 2026 comparative study of AI code sandbox engines finds runc/Docker has the largest attack surface, Firecracker the lowest CVE velocity, and rootless container runtimes still carry privilege-escalation risk.

sources.title: Docker docs — Seccomp security profiles
sources.claim: Docker's default seccomp profile blocks roughly 44 of 300+ syscalls including mount, unshare, keyctl, bpf, ptrace and the kernel-module calls.

sources.title: Datadog Security Labs — Container security fundamentals, part 6
sources.claim: In a default Docker container unshare fails with Operation not permitted because of the seccomp filter; CVE-2022-0185 needed that syscall.

sources.title: NVISO Labs — Rootless containers with Podman
sources.claim: Podman has no long-running privileged daemon; rootless Podman maps container UID 0 to the invoking user's host UID, so an escape yields that user's privileges rather than root.

sources.title: OneUptime — Rootless pods and SELinux confinement on RHEL 9
sources.claim: Podman labels container processes container_t by default and rootless containers get the same SELinux confinement as rootful ones, a layer rootless Docker lacks.

sources.title: anthropics/claude-code — .devcontainer/devcontainer.json
sources.claim: The reference devcontainer adds NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW via runArgs, bind-mounts only the workspace as /workspace, keeps ~/.claude and shell history in per-devcontainer named volumes, runs as remoteUser node, and applies the firewall in postStartCommand.

sources.title: anthropics/claude-code — .devcontainer/Dockerfile
sources.claim: The reference Dockerfile is node:20, installs iptables/ipset/gh/jq, copies init-firewall.sh as root-owned and grants the node user a single NOPASSWD sudo rule for it.

sources.title: Pro Custodibus — WireGuard in Podman
sources.claim: Running iptables inside a rootless Podman container needs both NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW, and the xt_/iptable_ kernel modules must be loaded on the host beforehand because module loading requires real root.

sources.title: containers/podman issue #12661 — modprobe ip_tables not permitted
sources.claim: In an unprivileged Podman context an iptables/modprobe call fails with Operation not permitted when the needed netfilter module is not already loaded on the host.

sources.title: moby/moby issue #45919 — rootless bind mounts owned by root
sources.claim: Under rootless Docker, bind-mounted host files owned by the invoking user appear as root-owned inside the container, so a non-root container user cannot write the mounted repo.

sources.title: OneUptime — Using --userns=keep-id with Podman
sources.claim: Podman's --userns=keep-id maps the host UID/GID straight through into the container, eliminating bind-mount permission mismatches in rootless mode.

sources.title: Sean Heath — VS Code Dev Containers with rootless Podman
sources.claim: Driving VS Code Dev Containers off rootless Podman requires pointing the extension at the podman binary and adding --userns=keep-id plus containerUser/updateRemoteUserUID to devcontainer.json.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Network configuration
sources.claim: Claude Code's documented egress requirements are api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, claude.com, platform.claude.com, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com, downloads.claude.ai, storage.googleapis.com, bridge.claudeusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, code.claude.com, two Datadog intake hosts, formulae.brew.sh, plus registry.npmjs.org for npm installs; it honours HTTPS_PROXY and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS but not SOCKS.

sources.title: Docker docs — Compose file networks reference
sources.claim: Compose's internal: true creates an externally isolated network with no external connectivity.

sources.title: OneUptime — Docker's embedded DNS server
sources.claim: Docker's embedded resolver at 127.0.0.11 forwards any name it cannot answer locally to the host's upstream resolvers, so DNS still leaves the box even from an isolated network unless you override the resolver.

sources.title: Podman docs — podman-network-create
sources.claim: podman network create --internal restricts external access on the network and disables the DNS name plugin for it.

sources.title: mattolson/agent-sandbox
sources.claim: agent-sandbox pairs a mitmproxy sidecar with in-container iptables so only the proxy is reachable, mounts secrets into the proxy only, and warns that an IDE's devcontainer management channel is a control plane outside the firewall.

sources.title: HackTricks — Abusing the Docker socket for privilege escalation
sources.claim: Mounting the Docker socket into a container is equivalent to granting host root, because the container can start a --privileged container.

sources.title: SentinelOne — CVE-2026-6406
sources.claim: CVE-2026-6406 let the Docker CLI --use-api-socket flag smuggle the Docker socket past Docker Desktop's Enhanced Container Isolation because the policy check inspected only HostConfig.Binds, not HostConfig.Mounts.

sources.title: VS Code docs — Sharing git credentials with your container
sources.claim: VS Code Dev Containers copies the host .gitconfig into the container, reuses the host credential helper, and forwards the host SSH agent automatically.

sources.title: The Hacker News — Claude Code flaws allow remote code execution
sources.claim: Three disclosed Claude Code flaws (including CVE-2025-59536 and CVE-2026-21852) achieved command execution or API-key exfiltration purely from repository-local config files such as .claude/settings.json and .mcp.json.

sources.title: Hacker News — containing Claude Code
sources.claim: Practitioner discussion on containing Claude Code centres on the official devcontainer, ad-hoc firejail scripts, and Docker's microVM sandboxes product.

sources.title: Development Containers specification
sources.claim: The Dev Containers specification defines devcontainer.json as a portable description of a development environment.

sources.title: devcontainers/cli
sources.claim: The devcontainer CLI is the editor-independent reference implementation of the spec, so devcontainer.json can be driven from a plain terminal.

sources.title: Docker docs — Sandboxes
sources.claim: Docker Desktop's sandboxes feature provisions a microVM with its own Docker daemon and workspace sync as a stronger-than-container option.

sources.title: agentcage/agentcage
sources.claim: agentcage is MIT-licensed and ships a pluggable inspector chain over every request, WebSocket frame and DNS query, with allowlist/blocklist dnsmasq modes resolving denied domains to placeholder IPs.
